svg.title: Poetry anthology
svg.desc: Nature and childhood: The Schoolboy: fear restricts natural growth. Wordsworth: remembered nature restores joy. Blackberry Picking: desired pleasure gives way to decay. Compare who or what causes change: authority, recollection or time. Home and the past: I Shall Return: homeland remembered; return hoped for. Drummer Hodge: burial abroad makes separation permanent. Place can preserve identity or expose distance from it. Compare the endings, not just landscape words. Love and distance: Sonnet 29: thoughts must give way to the real beloved. Dusting the Phone: imagined contact becomes anxious dependence. Cousin Kate: rejection and public judgement meet maternal pride. Compare power and the speaker’s final position. Family and selfhood: Catrin: connection survives conflict over independence. Origin Story: imperfect parental love can leave a valuable legacy. Both look back, but from different generations. A shared theme does not mean the same attitude. War beyond the battlefield: Disabled: injury and neglected homecoming. Kamikaze: survival followed by exclusion. Remains: a violent event persists in memory. Distinguish physical loss, social punishment and psychological harm. Looking and responsibility: War Photographer: witness, editor and audience respond differently. Decomposition: an observer rethinks making art from hardship. For every poem: voice → changing ideas → language/form/structure → relevant context. Compare effects with evidence.
